title: Number theory
audience: a college student in a mathematics degree program (or a related major such as physics, computer science or economics), or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn elementary number theory with computation: divisibility and the Euclidean algorithm, primes and unique factorization, congruences and the Chinese remainder theorem, Fermat's and Euler's theorems, public-key cryptography, primitive roots, primality tests and factoring, quadratic residues and quadratic reciprocity, continued fractions and Pell's equation, and arithmetic functions and the distribution of primes, with Python throughout.
primary_reading: Elementary Number Theory: Primes, Congruences, and Secrets by William Stein (free PDF)

weeks.1: Divisibility, the Euclidean algorithm and Bézout's identity
weeks.2: Primes and the fundamental theorem of arithmetic
weeks.4: Linear congruences and the Chinese remainder theorem
weeks.5: Fermat's little theorem, Euler's theorem and fast exponentiation
weeks.9: Quadratic residues and the Legendre symbol
weeks.12: Arithmetic functions, the prime number theorem and open problems

blocks.deliverable: Implement the extended Euclidean algorithm and prove that it is correct.
Solve systems of congruences by hand and in code.
Encrypt and decrypt with a toy RSA key and explain why decryption works.
Week 7 midterm; implement a probabilistic primality test.
Use quadratic reciprocity to decide whether supplied congruences are solvable.
Solve a Pell equation with continued fractions.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Number theory toolkit: write a tested plain-Python library with the extended Euclidean algorithm, modular inverses, the Chinese remainder theorem, fast modular exponentiation, the Miller–Rabin test, Pollard's rho method and continued fractions, use it to build a toy RSA key and to factor a deliberately weak one, and write a report that proves each algorithm correct and explains what makes real keys secure.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
